candidates.source_summary: Our player ratings from the EFL Trophy clash with League Two side Rochdale
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Doncaster Rovers came from behind to secure a well-deserved 4-1 victory away at Rochdale, securing their place in the knockout stages of the EFL Trophy in the process. Grant McCann made nine changes from the team that was thrashed away at MK Dons on Saturday. Josh Clarke was selected in goal, Jay McGrath and Tom Nixon returned to the defence while there was also opportunities for the likes of Harry Clifton, Darren Robinson, Bayley McCann and Brandon Hanlan among others. Jack Senior and Sean Grehan were the only players to keep their place in the starting lineup. Doncaster Rovers got off to a challenging start and were forced into an early change after just three minutes when new arrival Will Keane was forced off with an injury. Hanlan could and probably should have put Rovers in the driving seat moments later, but was denied by a strong save by Sam Waller. Matters got worse after 15 minutes when the hosts took an early lead, latching on to a mistake from Sean Grehan, which allowed Ian Henderson to easily tap home from close-range on his record-breaking 532nd appearance for the Dale. McCann’s men made more changes at the break, introducing both Owen Bailey and Jordan Thomas in an effort to rejuvenate their hopes of progressing to the next stage of the competition and it very much worked the trick. Rovers levelled proceedings in the 54th minute through Alfie May’s close distance strike after great work from Clifton in the build-up. The Vikings then the took the lead nine minutes later when Hanlan netted his first of the season from close range after some brilliant work by both McGrath and Thomas. Bailey, who was brought on to play centre-back in the second half, put the game to bed with a close-range finish in the 88th minute, capping off a true captain’s performance from the 27-year-old. Subsitute Isaac Hutchinson then topped off a great day for the visitors with a goal from close distance. Here are our player ratings from Doncaster Rovers’ final EFL Trophy group stage game.

candidates.source_summary: The landowner has instructed a contractor to survey the grounds of the former Turner Brother's factory to locate asbestos
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A derelict factory in Rochdale was once the world’s largest producer of asbestos – a toxic material which has led to the death of thousands in the UK. Now the owner of the old Turner Brothers factory in Spotland will carry out investigations to locate where the asbestos has been buried. Spodden Park Ltd, who own the 75-acre site, say the asbestos won’t be disturbed during the work. The contractor carrying out the works will provide a better understanding of the landscape so when the site clean up does happen, it can be done safely. To get the very latest from Manchester's political scene in your newsfeed - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source Locals have shared pictures of workers in overalls and diggers at the site recently. That could be connected to the clearance of knotweed. Spodden Park Ltd intends to remediate the area off Spod Road in order to redevelop it. Although their future vision for the area off Spod Road has not been revealed, it is understood there is an ambition to build housing and create a park in some capacity. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. A spokesperson for Spodden Park said: “Over the next few weeks, a specialist contractor will undertake investigation works across the site. These investigations will enable us to better understand ground conditions across the site, including the location of asbestos beneath the ground. This will inform the safest and most appropriate remediation strategy. “During these investigations, no asbestos will be disturbed and no buildings or structures will be demolished. To carry out these works, heavy machinery will be operating on site. Some breaking of concrete may be required; however, the concrete itself does not contain asbestos.” In their recent update on their works on the site, Spodden Park has also issued another warning, urging trespassers not to set foot on the grounds. The site, nicknamed ‘ Rochdale ’s Chernobyl’ due to the toxic nature of the materials that used to be produced there, is off-limits to the public. Only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ have dared step through the barbed gates to get a hands-on view of the decaying set of buildings and overgrown vegetation on the site. The landowners say they’ve installed more security measures in order to prevent more break ins. candidates.source_body_excerpt: UK Lawyers for Israel (UKLFI) has challenged a Rochdale leisure centre over its treatment of an Israeli gym member who was allegedly subjected to racist abuse and threats of violence, only to be told that he and his fiancée could be banned from the gym alongside the alleged aggressor. UKLFI has written to the management of Oulder Hill Leisure Complex in Rochdale, warning that its handling of the incident may breach the Equality Act 2010 and appears to contradict its own rules on discriminatory and threatening behaviour. The incident began on 19 June 2026 when a gym member was asked by another customer where he came from. When he replied that he was from Israel, the man allegedly launched into a tirade of racist abuse. According to the Israeli, the man shouted: “F*** you, you are killing babies. I hate all the people of Israel.” He then allegedly declared: “F*** you, I wish I had a button I could press right now and I would kill all you people from Israel,” before threatening: “I could f*** you up right now.” The Israeli, who had recently signed up for a year’s membership, immediately reported the incident to gym staff, explaining that he no longer felt safe around the individual. He also reported the matter to the police on 23 June. However, the alleged aggressor continued to use the gym. On 24 August, after noticing the man staring aggressively at him, the Israeli approached him in an attempt to resolve the situation peacefully. He suggested that they put the previous incident behind them and agree that nothing further would happen. Instead, the man allegedly called him a “baby killer” again and swore at him.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: The borough blossomed with success at this year’s North West in Bloom awards, celebrating a bumper crop of 21 gold awards and eight overall category wins. The outstanding results were announced at the annual awards ceremony at the Toughsheet Community Stadium in Bolton last week, following Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) judges visiting in the summer. The awards recognise the borough’s success in horticulture, environmental responsibility, recycling, biodiversity, cleanliness and community participation. Following the outstanding gold achievement and scooping the overall Town Centres and City Centres title at the recent Royal Horticultural Society Britain in Bloom awards, Rochdale town centre’s horticulturists remained on their winning streak taking gold and best in category for both their Small City and Town Centre entries in the local in bloom awards. Rochdale in Bloom treasurer Phil Massey also received an outstanding contribution award for his significant work supporting Rochdale’s success in both national and local efforts. Baillie Street Quarter won the new Best Art in the Community award for outstanding artwork from the recent Common Walls International Mural Festival, organised by talented local artist Hayley Garner. Rochdale BID also secured gold and won the Best Business Improvement District (BID) category, adding to Rochdale’s achievements following its designation as Greater Manchester’s Town of Culture for 2025/26. candidates.source_summary: Rochdale council and Hopwood DePree went head to head in a High Court trial in September. But the next steps for the historic hall is are yet to be determined
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Just over a month on from the High Court battle over Hopwood Hall, the door has been left open for reconciliation. Hopwood DePree, an American filmmaker who wanted to buy the historic landmark from Rochdale Council, had entered an option agreement with the council to restore the hall back in 2017, until that agreement was terminated by the council in October 2024. Since then, Mr DePree, who claims ancestral connections with the 1400s stately home, has felt he had a legally binding agreement to purchase Hopwood Hall for £1. However, in September, following a two-day trial in Manchester Civil Justice Centre, the court ruled that the council was not acting unlawfully when it ended the exclusivity agreement with the American filmmaker. To get the very latest from Manchester's political scene in your newsfeed - click here to add the MEN as your preferred Google source The High Court found that the ‘change of use’ planning approval granted in 2022 wasn’t enough to trigger the option to purchase the hall for a ‘peppercorn fee’ – £1. Therefore, Mr DePree’s claim was lost. Now, the filmmaker has issued an open letter to town hall bosses to set out his terms for a resolution discussion. This comes after council leader Neil Emmott told the latest town hall meeting his ‘door is always open’ to Mr DePree. He added that if Mr DePree came back with a viable plan for the future of Hopwood Hall, the council would listen. Both sides have said a costly court battle could have been avoided. But Mr DePree’s latest open letter to the local authority suggested it was the council that took ‘an incredibly aggressive legal route of termination and locking them out of Hopwood Hall’. The council has always maintained that the volunteer group was barred due to safety reasons. The reasons for the ending of the agreement by the council and being booted out of the hall are still something Mr DePree says he doesn’t understand. The US-born adopted Middletonian wants to see the council release documents about communications between authorities about how they handled dealings about the hall; commission an independent review; correct inaccurate public statements about his community-led effort; and to pause further action in the ongoing legal proceedings and enter into discussions to find an amicable solution. In his letter, he said: “I hope we can find an amicable resolution for Hopwood Hall. At the October 15, 2026 public council meeting, you stated that your ‘door is always open’ and ‘Rochdale council is willing to listen’ if I come forward with a sustainable plan, following the council’s unexpected termination of our community-led rescue in 2024. “I would welcome constructive discussions but they must begin with a clear explanation of why our previous proposal was rejected. Nearly two years after our heritage team was locked out, the council still has not provided meaningful answers and continues to refuse to release documents and communications about decisions taken. “Despite our challenges, I remain open to constructive dialogue, including an independently moderated public forum where councillors, volunteers and residents can address concerns and explore Hopwood Hall’s future. “Given the time-sensitive nature of our legal options, we must reserve our rights. However, this should not prevent prompt, productive discussion aimed at reaching a resolution without further litigation. Littleborough improved to gold in Large Town, as did Wardle Village in its category, while Pennines in Bloom retained gold. candidates.source_summary: ‘Go as far as we can - Cliff Byrne looks ahead to Doncaster Rovers’ EFL Trophy clash with Rochdale Doncaster Free Press
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Doncaster Rovers assistant coach Cliff Byrne believes Tuesday night’s EFL Trophy clash with Rochdale gives the players the perfect chance to try and rectify some of the problems that were apparent during last Saturday’s 6-1 defeat to MK Dons. Rovers go into their final group stage game in second position with a record of three points from their opening two matches. Grant McCann’s men were beaten 3-1 by Huddersfield Town in the first game before more recently recording a 1-0 win over Liverpool Under-21s. It means they are firmly on course to reach the knockout stages of the competition provided they can pick up all three points or either equal or better Liverpool Under-21’s result against Huddersfield. Rochdale are currently on one point. They drew 3-3 with Liverpool Under-21s before losing on penalties in the first match before falling to a disappointing 5-0 defeat against Huddersfield. Reflecting on the weekend, Byrne told club media: “It was a game that was important that we looked back over and looked through and it's a game we have to quickly learn from. “So our benefit now is we’ve got a game coming quickly, so we’re looking forward to that and to be able to go and put a performance on, it’s a game we need to win, it’s a cup competition and we want to progress to the next round, so that’s where the focus is.” Byrne continued: “I think when you come off a poor defeat and a poor performance couple with it, you definitely want an opportunity to go and rectify it and put it right, so when you have a game within a couple of days, that gives you the opportunity to go and do that and that’s exactly what we’ll be aiming to do.” Rovers reached the semi-final of this competition and only narrowly missed out on a first visit to Wembley since 2008 after losing to Stockport County in the semi-final. The South Yorkshire side have only ever won this competition once. That came in 2007 when Sean O’Driscoll’s men were triumphant over Bristol Rovers at the Millenium Stadium. “We want to go as far as we can,” said Byrne. “We made no bones about it last season and this season we have had some really good teams in our group, we’re down to the last game and it’s in our hands to progress to the next round.” The EFL Trophy is often seen as a competition for youngsters and squad players to get an opportunity. Byrne hinted that they’ll be some changes but also emphasized the importance of picking up a good result. He said: “It’s a game we want to win and the selection we have in mind is for that, to win the game and progress. “But there may be an opportunity for some players to get more minutes than they have in recent weeks but I think that's the nature of how the schedule is. It’s very hard to ask the same 11 to go time and time again. They’ll be opportunities in some areas but in others there won’t be.”

candidates.source_summary: Planners' refusal of a bid to turn a former care home into university accommodation has been upheld.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: An appeal over plans to turn a former care home into university accommodation has been dismissed. The Al Sadiq Academy appealed to the Planning Inspectorate after Rochdale Council refused permission to change the use of the former Briarmede care home, in Rochdale Road, Middleton, into university accommodation. The plans included creating 11 en-suite bedrooms, with kitchens and dining hall/games room, library, study rooms, computer rooms and toilets on the ground floor. Planning offices recommended approval for the application, which would have included conditions the building is solely for the use of residents and was not used to provide classes, education services or private or community events at any time. But the application was called in by the council’s planning committee which refused it following concerns about the need for the facility, and the impact it would have on neighbours. In delivering the appeal decision, planning inspector K Mee said: “The main issues are whether the appeal site is a suitable location having regard to the local development plan, insofar as it relates to the type of accommodation; and the effect of the proposed development on the character of the surrounding area and the living conditions of neighbouring residents, with regard to noise and disturbance. “The appellant identifies a number of higher education institutions across Greater Manchester, including Hopwood Hall College opposite the appeal site, as potential sources of demand for student accommodation. “However, no substantive evidence has been provided to demonstrate that these institutions have been consulted regarding the proposals, nor that there is an identified unmet need for additional student accommodation either locally or across the wider area.

candidates.source_summary: The green light has been given for Storage World to be rebuilt in Middleton town centre.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The green light has been given for Storage World to be rebuilt in Middleton town centre. Rochdale Council has approved Self-Storage Performance Management International Ltd’s planning application to replace the building in Old Hall Street after it was destroyed by fire in June last year. Instead of a like-for-like replacement, SSPMI will now create a £12 million smaller, taller, mixed-use building with self-storage units on the upper floors and commercial units on the ground floor. The new building will occupy half the footprint of the former Storage World units, but will include two extra storeys to deliver the same capacity inside. In documents submitted with the application, P4 Planning said: “The applicant’s key objective following the catastrophic fire is to replace the building with a suitable modern design that will bring back SME business activity and self-storage space as quickly as possible. “Through close engagement with the council planning and other departments, the applicant is keen to deliver a far better development, with a more appropriate design and format that will also bring wider regeneration benefits. “The mix of uses and economic benefits, design and wider potential benefits will all have a positive impact on the future regeneration of Middleton town centre. “The scale, mass and materials draw reference from the historic research and the site’s past, when Albany Mill was present on the site until 1975.”

Vale had only found the net six times in their previous 11 League Two games but, after Onel Hernandez put them ahead 90 seconds in, George Byers’ penalty and a third from Jordan Gabriel put them 3-0 up inside 22 minutes. Keyrol Figueroa scored Vale’s fourth late on, either side of the visitors’ goals, and Brady focused on a fine day for them. “First off we were very clinical in what we did,” he said. “We created loads of chances and the way we played, especially in that first half, was really pleasing. “To concede those two is disappointing but I want to focus on the positives. We’ve scored four goals at home, three from open play. Some of the delivery, some of our play was really positive today. “Onel stood out for me, he was excellent, his movement was great for the first goal and the way he finished it was brilliant. Then to get the penalty really made a difference after breaking through their back line and Gabby following up well after a great strike from Demo (Kyle Dempsey). At the end it’s great work from George Hall and Figgy knows where the back of the net is. “We’ve got to keep looking forward, we’ve been in tough situations, we said last week (defeat at York) had to be just a bump in the road and we’ve bounced back this week. I’m really pleased with the group, with everyone.” After his side shipped five against Accrington last week, Dale boss Ian Watson had watched in horror as they conceded three early goals.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Emergency services descended on a road in Rochdale after a car smashed into a house and caused a gas leak. Greater Manchester Police said they were called to reports of a vehicle colliding with a property on Halifax Road at around 2.55am this morning, Saturday, October 31. The collision went on to cause a confirmed gas leak, the force said. Up to 55 people were evacuated following the incident and a 50 metre cordon was put in place whilst investigations were ongoing. Posting on social media this morning, Greater Manchester Police for Rochdale said: "Emergency services are responding to an incident on Halifax Road, Rochdale, following a vehicle collision with a property at around 2:25am which has caused a confirmed gas leak. "Around 55 people have been evacuated and a 50-metre cordon is in place. The road remains closed while emergency services carry out their work." A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said: “Shortly after 2.25am on Saturday 31 October, three fire engines from Rochdale and Littleborough fire stations attended a road traffic collision involving one car on Halifax Road, Rochdale. "Crews arrived quickly and used specialist equipment to make the area safe. Two casualties were taken to hospital by North West Ambulance Service. “Firefighters also assisted with the evacuation of nearby properties because of a gas leak caused by the collision. “Overall, crews were in attendance for approximately four-and-a-half hours.”

candidates.source_summary: The financial and practical challenges surrounding the borough's school places will be highlighted in each town next week.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The financial and practical challenges surrounding the borough’s school places will be highlighted in each town next week. Rochdale Council’s township committees will hear that the lowest birth rate for 23 years is expected to present a “significant challenge” for the long-term financial sustainability of some primary schools within the borough — while 2027 is expected to see the highest number of students apply for the area’s secondary schools. A report to be presented to Heywood, Pennines, Middleton, Rochdale North and Rochdale South township committees reveals that the borough’s birth rate has seen a peak in Reception year pupils arriving in school in September, 2026, but, the birth rate for the intake in 2027 is 2,647 — the lowest since 2003. The report said: “A small number of schools have seen too many empty seats over the last few years as intake numbers reduced and a low intake in 2027 is going to see additional financial pressures on those schools. “Current birth rates indicate a steady but slow rise in the years to 2030. The current projected intake for 2030 is approximately 2,900 and includes children from new housing developments across the borough.” In September, 2024, 90 surplus Reception places were removed, followed by an additional 35 for September, 2025. The report warns that further reductions are needed in some areas of the borough where there are too many empty places. While recent years have seen an average of 113 children needing places after moving into the borough each year, this figure has fallen to 20 over the past two years. As well as fewer children entering primary schools, there has been an average of 30 pupils per year not taking up secondary school places within the borough.
candidates.source_title: Schools face financial challenges over pupil places - Rochdale Times

Note: Due to a holiday (and limited wifi) Rob's match report is minimal for this game. If you want to expand on the report please add your comments at the end Manager Jon Brady made four changes from the game against Manchester City including the return of attacking duo Onel Hernandez and Max Watters. The duo combined to give Vale an early goal. Watters headed down a ball to Dempsey and his delightful dinked pass found Hernandez who beat the keeper. It was 1-0 after just two minutes. The second arrived just nine minutes later. Aidan Flint clipped Hernandez in the box and captain George Byers made no mistake from the resulting penalty kick. It was 3-0 on 22 minutes when the Rochdale keeper kept out Dempsey's fierce drive but Gabriel was on hand to convert the loose ball. It could have been more - with Watters heading one delightful move over the bar - but at the break the Valiants were comfortably ahead. The second-half was a different affair. Vale swopped the front duo and Rochdale made a host of changes. It resulted in the visitors having much more of the ball and although they created chances they could not beat Marosi in the Vale goal until 82 minutes when veteran Ian Henderson found the target. That was a blot on Vale's copybook but the Valiants countered with another goal for loanee Keyrol Figueroa. He latched on to a good cross from the impressive George Hall to restore Vale's three goal advantage. In the closing moments, Rochdale added a second. Marosi produced a great save from a header but the rebound was put away by Tasker. However, it was too little, too late. The first-half display was good while the second 45 minutes may not have been great at times. So, it was a game of two halves but this was still a decent victory for Vale and one which eases the pressure on manager Jon Brady. Full-time: Port Vale 4-2 Rochdale

candidates.source_body_excerpt: An emphatic first-half performance saw the Valiants cruise to victory against Rochdale for a fourth league win of the season. An all-action first half, in the most part from a Vale persuasion, provided a goal just two minutes in. Max Watters chested a ball down to Kyle Dempsey who played a neat through ball to Onel Hernandez, who took a touch and shot across his body into the bottom right corner for an early home lead. The visitors, who had conceded five to Accrington Stanley the week before continued to struggle, as eight minutes later Hernandez was tripped in the box. The man with the armband, George Byers, tucked into the bottom corner for his third goal from the spot this season and Vale’s second. Rochdale’s only real threatening moment of the first half came when ex-Valiant Dajaune Brown was sent through, but a spectacular last-ditch block from Jasper Moon retained the two-goal lead. Two minutes after, Kyle Dempsey, in acres of space, rifled a shot towards Dale keeper Walker, who parried out to Jordan Gabriel who reacted first and passed home to make it three in front of a jubilant Vale Park. Great chances kept coming for Jon Brady’s side, with George Hall, who was a bright spark throughout, involved in the creation of more chances in the latter stages of the half.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Three early goals saw Port Vale ease to a 4-2 win at home to Rochdale in League Two. The Valiants had only hit six goals in 11 league games but with some dismal Dale defending they virtually sealed victory after 22 minutes. Onel Hernandez opened the scoring inside 90 seconds, gathering Kyle Dempsey’s through-ball and finding the bottom corner. Vale doubled their lead after 11 minutes. Aden Flint tripped Hernandez and George Byers fired the resulting penalty past Sam Waller. Dale threatened momentarily when Cian Hayes sent former Vale striker Dajaune Brown through, but he was thwarted by Jasper Moon. Moments later Vale scored their third. Dempsey’s shot was parried by Waller and Jordan Gabriel reacted first to slot home the rebound. With the game over as a contest, the second half produced few chances but ended with a flurry of goals. Dale’s Ian Henderson headed in after 82 minutes before Keyrol Figueroa restored Vale’s three-goal cushion with a simple tap-in four minutes from time.

As we have said before in Faith News, we have decided to sell some of our youth group costumes as they are taking up a lot of space in the church. We still have many boxes of costumes to sell and have been exceptionally lucky, because when we decided to dispose of some costumes we found that societies throughout the world were interested in buying some. There are also some backcloths available too. We have sold some to societies in Germany, Italy, Norway, and America - not bad for a little church in Littleborough. Indeed, our first Joseph and the first Wizard of Oz costumes were sold to professional theatre companies in England, but our The King and I costumes have gone to an American company.

candidates.source_summary: Empty and neglected buildings across the borough could be brought back into use with help from £2.24 million from the Government’s new Derelict Buildings Fund.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Empty and neglected buildings across the borough could be brought back into use with help from £2.24 million from the Government’s new Derelict Buildings Fund. Rochdale Council’s allocation, confirmed alongside Wednesday’s Budget, is part of a £125 million national fund to help councils transform derelict buildings into spaces their communities need. The money can be used to buy derelict buildings, close the viability gaps that stop regeneration schemes going ahead, and help community groups and local businesses take buildings over. Rochdale MP Paul Waugh will act as a Programme Champion for the fund. Government guidance will make clear that councils should work alongside local MPs when deciding which buildings and projects to back. The announcement comes as communities across the borough fight to save their locals. In Littleborough, there is strong interest in reopening The Wheatsheaf, part of the Grade II listed Roundhouse building dating from the early 1860s, which closed in June. Earlier this month, Rochdale Council passed a motion brought by Littleborough Lakeside Councillor Richard Jackson calling on the Government to block restrictive covenants on pub sales. Mr Waugh has supported this campaign directly having written to ministers urging action. These covenants allow pub companies selling a building to ban it from ever being used as a pub again, a restriction that binds every future owner. candidates.source_summary: There are a few telltale signs which tell you Charlie Tasker has settled quickly and made a good early impression on loan a long way from home at Rochdale.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: There are a few telltale signs which tell you Charlie Tasker has settled quickly and made a good early impression on loan a long way from home at Rochdale. Like the fact he has been a regular for the League Two outfit and has been entrusted with a new role on the left. Like the way the fans have taken to him and the club are happy for him to talk to a reporter from far-off Brighton even after a 5-0 home defeat. Or like the way he hasn't been back to Mile Oak yet and speaks about how he is enjoying not Manchester but "Manny". He isn't quite speaking like Danny Welbeck yet but the 20-year-old right-back is relishing his first EFL challenge after leaving Albion under-21s early in the season. Speaking after a session at Rochdale's training base near the site of Manchester City's old Maine Road home, he told The Argus: "This is my first loan, so I wanted to go somewhere where you think you have got a good chance of playing. "You know you are never guaranteed minutes in football. "But, when people were talking about Rochdale, when I spoke to the manager on the call, they play really attractive football. Similar to Brghton, actually.
candidates.source_title: Albion prospect enjoying a new life and new role after big loan move to North West
